newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PARL'T REJECTS SOCIALDEMS PROPOSAL ON BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PARL'T REJECTS SOCIALDEMS PROPOSAL ON BUDGET.

text.p: The Czech lower house has rejected a plan by the opposition Social Democrats which would have forced a reworking of the government's 1997 draft budget, thus opening the way for a possible vote on the draft later on Wednesday.

The parliament rejected a series of votes on the plan as four deputies split from the opposition -- including Budget Chairman Jozef Wagner of the Social Democrats (CSSD) -- to vote with the centre-right coalition in killing the CSSD proposal.
The CSSD plan, if approved would have forced the government to re-work its draft 1997 balanced budget before the end of October.

It would have limited the government to changes during the fiscal year of a maximum five percent on the revenue side and five percent on the expenditure side of the total volume of the agreed state budget.

It would have also required a rise in payments to municipalities to compensate for changes in the tax code, and would limit the mayors of major cities to determine discressionary spending of up to a maximum of 10 percent of state funds.

The centre-right coalition, which lost its majority in the house in June elections, has hinted it might resign if the opposition, led by the Social Democrats, succeeded in forcing changes to its planned balanced budget.
It is not yet clear if the first reading of the 1997 budget will make it to the floor later on Wednesday.
